turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to her every wish and ensure that their eldest son was married as she desired, for her peace of mind.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband if he would promise to care for their children and ensure their future, emphasizing her concern that they should not be burdened by the past.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would do everything in his power to make her wishes come true and that he would always remember her teachings.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband if he would see to it that the marriage of their eldest son was arranged properly, without delay, as she wished.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would arrange the marriage of their eldest son with all due haste and see to it that their family's future was secure, as she wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung to ensure that the eldest son's wife was treated with kindness and respect, as a daughter of the household.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would see to it that the eldest son's wife was treated with the utmost kindness and respect, ensuring she felt at home in their family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung also ensure that the eldest son was guided to make good decisions, so their family could prosper.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would guide their eldest son with wisdom and care, ensuring the family's prosperity and honour.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she hoped her son would find happiness in his marriage and that the family would remain strong and united.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would do everything in his power to ensure her son's happiness and the family's unity, promising that their love and strength would endure.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung must ensure the eldest son's wife was well taken care of and that she felt accepted in the family, her voice soft but firm with a hint of urgency.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would ensure the eldest son's wife felt welcomed and cherished, promising to treat her as one of the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she wished to see the wedding preparations underway soon, her eyes filled with determination despite her frailty.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do his best to ensure the wedding preparations proceeded smoothly, his voice trembling slightly with the weight of his mother’s wishes and his father’s expectations.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would oversee the wedding preparations personally, ensuring every detail was perfect and that the eldest son’s wife felt embraced by the family.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan and Wang Lung that she would personally oversee the preparations for the eldest son’s wife, ensuring that everything was done to the highest standard and that the new wife felt at home.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the wedding must be a celebration of joy and love, assuring O-lan that her wishes would be fulfilled with the utmost care and devotion.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the preparations must reflect the family's gratitude towards the eldest son’s wife and her family, her voice steady despite the pain.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan and the eldest son that he would ensure the wedding preparations were not only a reflection of gratitude but also a celebration of love and unity, insisting that every aspect would be handled with care and precision.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
